title: Baron’s reconciliation: two fiducial acts — one before justification, one after
source_text: LXII. Ut autem istud conciliat cum doctrina Articuli decimi octavi a nobis exposita, monet se propterea non negare quod fideles habeant ejusmodi fiduciam veniae impetratae per meritum Christi: aut quod haec fiducia non sit fidei salvificae actus: sed hoc solum se velle, quod fiducia illa veniae impetratae non sit ille actus fidei qui est causa instrumentalis justificationis nostrae; quoniam est natura posterior justificationi, & quid eam consequens. Et postea sic de re tota concludit: De objecto igitur fidei salvificae haec tenenda sunt. Primo tenendum est, objectum fiduciae non solum esse remissionem peccatorum impetrandam & obtinendam, sed etiam eorum remissionem jam impetratam. Secundo, fiduciam in haec duo tendere per duos distinctos actus, quorum alter praecedit justificationem, ut ejus causa instrumentalis; alter eam sequitur, ut ejus effectum & consequens. Tertio, actum fiducialem, qui justificationem praecedit, ut ejus causa, esse persuasionem de Christi satisfactione pro nobis in particulari, & de remissione peccatorum obtinenda per & propter ejus satisfactionem. Quarto, actum fiducialem, qui justificationem sequitur, esse persuasionem de remissione peccatorum jam impetrata, & de nostra perseverantia in eo statu, usque ad finem vitae. Denique in fine Articuli, ad quoddam Bellarmini argumentum respondens, dicit fidem justificantem praecedere justificationem, sed non secundum omnes ejus actus, quosdam enim actus fidei justificantis justificationem sequi. Et similiter fidem specialis misericordiae justificatione posteriorem esse, sed non secundum omnes ejus actus: etenim persuasionem de venia seu remissione peccatorum impetranda esse actum illius fidei, quam specialis misericordiae vocant: eam autem justificationem praecedere, saltem ordine naturae.
pass_a_gloss: But that he may reconcile this with the doctrine of the eighteenth Article set forth by us, he warns that he does not therefore deny that the faithful have such trust of pardon obtained through Christ's merit: or that this trust is not an act of saving faith: but that he only means that that trust of pardon obtained is not that act of faith which is the instrumental cause of our justification; since it is by nature posterior to justification, and something consequent upon it. And afterward he thus concludes concerning the whole matter: These things therefore are to be held concerning the object of saving faith. First it is to be held that the object of trust is not only remission of sins to be obtained and gotten, but also their remission already obtained. Second, that trust tends to these two by two distinct acts, of which one precedes justification as its instrumental cause; the other follows it as its effect and consequent. Third, that the fiducial act which precedes justification as its cause is a persuasion concerning Christ's satisfaction for us in particular, and concerning remission of sins to be obtained through and for His satisfaction. Fourth, that the fiducial act which follows justification is a persuasion concerning remission of sins already obtained, and concerning our perseverance in that state unto the end of life. Finally at the end of the Article, answering a certain argument of Bellarmine, he says that justifying faith precedes justification, but not according to all its acts — for some acts of justifying faith follow justification. And likewise that faith of special mercy is posterior to justification, but not according to all its acts: for the persuasion concerning pardon or remission of sins to be obtained is an act of that faith which they call of special mercy: but that it precedes justification, at least in the order of nature.
pass_b_english: Already-obtained-pardon fiducia can be a saving-faith act — but not the instrumental cause (it follows justification).
Object of fiducia: both remission to-be-obtained and already-obtained.
Before: persuasion of Christ’s satisfaction for me + remission to be obtained.
After: persuasion of remitted sins + perseverance to life’s end.
Not all acts of justifying / special-mercy faith precede justification.
